description: Progressive-clue identification game. Each item is a figure (answerKind 'person') or a thing (answerKind 'thing'); clues run vague to specific and are revealed one at a time. Every item carries at least one authoritative citation, same rule as the question bank.

clues: As an infant I was hidden, then drawn out of the water and raised in a household not my own.
In exile I met God in a bush that burned without being consumed.
I was sent back to demand freedom for a people enslaved for generations.
On a mountain I received the Law written by God's own finger.
I led the people forty years through the desert but did not myself enter the promised land.
items.explanation: Moses led Israel out of Egypt and mediated the covenant at Sinai; the Catechism presents him as a foreshadowing of Christ the one Mediator.

clues: I was the youngest of my brothers, out watching the sheep when the prophet came to anoint me.
As a boy I faced a giant with a sling and five smooth stones.
I danced before the Ark of the Covenant as it entered my city.
I sinned gravely, then wrote a psalm of repentance that the Church still prays.
God promised that my throne and my house would endure forever.
items.explanation: David, Israel's great king and psalmist, is the ancestor and type of the Messiah; the Catechism calls him the model of prayer in repentance.

clues: My birth was announced to my father in the Temple, and he was struck silent until he named me.
I leapt in my mother's womb when the Mother of the Lord came to visit.
I lived in the wilderness, clothed in camel's hair, eating locusts and wild honey.
I baptized in the Jordan and told the crowds to prepare the way of the Lord.
Pointing to Him, I said, 'Behold, the Lamb of God.'
items.explanation: John the Baptist is the last of the prophets and the immediate precursor of the Lord, sent to prepare His way.

clues: I was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee when I was called to fish for men.
I walked on water toward the Lord, then began to sink when I doubted.
I confessed Him as the Christ, the Son of the living God.
He gave me a new name and the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
I denied Him three times before the cock crowed, then wept bitterly.
items.explanation: Simon Peter, given his name by Christ, is the rock on which the Church is built and the first among the apostles.

clues: I was a Pharisee, zealous for the Law, and I held the coats of those who stoned the first martyr.
On a road, a light from heaven threw me to the ground and a voice asked why I was persecuting Him.
I was blind for three days until a disciple laid hands on me.
I carried the Gospel across the Roman world and wrote letters to the churches I founded.
I called myself the least of the apostles, born out of due time.
items.explanation: Paul, once a persecutor, became the apostle to the Gentiles after his encounter with the risen Christ on the road to Damascus.

clues: My mother wept and prayed for my conversion for many years.
In my youth I chased pleasure and false philosophies, and prayed to be made chaste, but 'not yet.'
In a garden I heard a child's voice chanting 'take up and read.'
The bishop of Milan baptized me, and I became a bishop myself, in North Africa.
I wrote that our hearts are restless until they rest in God.
items.explanation: Augustine of Hippo, Doctor of the Church, recounts his conversion in the Confessions; the Catechism quotes his restless-heart prayer.

clues: I was one of the seven chosen to serve at table so the apostles could devote themselves to preaching.
I was full of grace and power and worked wonders among the people.
Brought before the council, my face was like the face of an angel.
As I was stoned, I saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand.
I died praying that the sin would not be held against my killers.
items.explanation: Stephen, a deacon, is the Church's first martyr; his dying prayer for his persecutors echoes Christ's own.

clues: I entered a Carmelite convent at fifteen and never left it.
I taught a 'little way' of trust and small acts of love rather than great deeds.
I died of tuberculosis at twenty-four, promising to spend my heaven doing good on earth.
My autobiography, Story of a Soul, was read around the world after my death.
Though I never left my cloister, I am a patroness of missionaries, and a Doctor of the Church.
items.explanation: Thérèse of Lisieux, the 'Little Flower,' taught that holiness is reached through confidence and love in ordinary things; the Catechism quotes her definition of prayer.

clues: An angel greeted me as 'full of grace' and told me not to be afraid.
I asked how this could be, since I had no husband, and was told the Holy Spirit would overshadow me.
I answered, 'Let it be done to me according to your word.'
I visited my kinswoman and sang that all generations would call me blessed.
At a wedding I told the servants, 'Do whatever He tells you.'
items.explanation: Mary's free 'yes' at the Annunciation made her the Mother of God; her fiat is the model of faith and obedience.

clues: I was a young deacon at a great council in 325 that met to answer a priest named Arius.
I spent much of my life as bishop of Alexandria, and was exiled five times for my stand.
The saying went that it was 'me against the world' when almost every see wavered.
I insisted the Son is of the same substance as the Father, not a creature.
I wrote that God became man so that man might become God by grace.
items.explanation: Athanasius defended the full divinity of Christ against Arianism, the teaching the Council of Nicaea condemned with the term consubstantial.

clues: I was the son of a great king and a king myself, and God appeared to me in a dream at Gibeon.
Offered anything, I asked not for long life or riches but for an understanding heart.
I settled a dispute between two women by proposing to divide a living child with a sword.
I built the Temple in Jerusalem, a house for the name of the Lord.
My later years were marked by foreign wives and the idolatry they drew me into.
items.explanation: Solomon, David's son, asked God for wisdom to govern and built the first Temple; his fall warns that wisdom is kept only by fidelity.

clues: The Lord had driven seven demons out of me.
I stood by the cross when most of the apostles had fled.
I came to the tomb while it was still dark and found the stone rolled away.
I mistook the risen Lord for the gardener until He spoke my name.
He sent me to announce the Resurrection to the apostles themselves.
items.explanation: Mary Magdalene was the first witness of the Resurrection and was sent by Christ to tell the apostles, earning the title 'apostle to the apostles.'

clues: I was instituted at a supper on the night before He died.
He said the bread was His body and the cup His blood, and told them to do this in memory of Him.
He had already promised that whoever eats this bread would live forever.
The Church calls me the source and summit of the whole Christian life.
Under the appearances of bread and wine, Christ is truly, really, and substantially present.
items.explanation: The Eucharist makes present the one sacrifice of Christ and gives His true Body and Blood; it is the source and summit of the Church's life.

clues: John administered a version of me in the Jordan, but mine as a sacrament came later.
The Lord's command was to make disciples of all nations by way of me, in the name of the Trinity.
I am the gateway to the other sacraments and cannot be repeated.
Through me, original sin and all personal sins are forgiven and one is born again of water and the Spirit.
I make a person a member of Christ and of His Church, and mark the soul permanently.
items.explanation: Baptism frees from sin, regenerates as a child of God, and incorporates into the Church; it is the necessary gateway to the sacramental life.

clues: I was built to exact measure from acacia wood and overlaid inside and out with gold.
Two golden cherubim faced each other above my cover, the mercy seat.
I carried the tablets of the Law, a jar of manna, and Aaron's staff that budded.
I went before the people into battle and around the walls of Jericho.
The Fathers see me fulfilled in the Virgin, who carried the Word made flesh.
items.explanation: The Ark held the signs of God's covenant and marked His presence among Israel; Christian tradition sees Mary as the new Ark, bearing Christ Himself.

clues: I am prayed on a string of beads divided into groups of ten.
My central prayer repeats an angel's greeting and a kinswoman's blessing, ending with a plea for prayers at the hour of death.
Each decade is joined to a scene from the life of Christ and His Mother, called a mystery.
There are now four sets of these mysteries: Joyful, Luminous, Sorrowful, and Glorious.
The Church commends me as a compendium of the whole Gospel prayed alongside Mary.
items.explanation: The Rosary meditates on the mysteries of Christ's life through vocal prayer centered on the Hail Mary; the Church holds it up as a summary of the Gospel.

clues: I was an instrument of Roman execution reserved for slaves and rebels.
The Lord told His followers they must take me up daily and follow Him.
On me the one sacrifice that takes away the sin of the world was offered.
St. Paul said I am folly to those perishing but the power of God to those being saved.
The Church venerates me solemnly once a year, on Good Friday.
items.explanation: The Cross is the altar of Christ's redeeming sacrifice; what the world counts as defeat is the power and wisdom of God.

clues: I am the central mystery of the Christian faith and of Christian life.
I am named whenever a person is baptized, and whenever the Sign of the Cross is made.
I am one God in three persons, distinct yet equal, each wholly God.
Reason alone cannot arrive at me; I am known only because God has revealed me.
items.explanation: The Trinity is one God in three coequal persons -- Father, Son, and Holy Spirit -- the deepest mystery of the faith, knowable only by revelation.

clues: I name an event, and my anniversary is celebrated nine months before Christmas.
By me the eternal Son took a human body and a human soul, without ceasing to be God.
The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us -- that is me.
St. Athanasius said God did me so that we might be made partakers of God.
items.explanation: In the Incarnation the Son of God assumed a full human nature; He is true God and true man in one person.

clues: I am a free and undeserved gift, not wages earned.
Baptism pours me into the soul; grave sin drives me out; the sacraments restore and increase me.
By me a person is made a partaker of the divine nature and an adopted child of God.
St. Paul said that by me you are saved, through faith, and this is not your own doing.
items.explanation: Sanctifying grace is God's own life given to the soul, making the person holy and a sharer in the divine nature.

clues: I was given on a mountain and written on two tablets of stone.
My first three words concern love of God; the remaining seven, love of neighbor.
The Lord summed me up in two: love God with all your heart, and your neighbor as yourself.
The Church numbers me as ten 'words,' and the Catechism devotes a major section to me.
items.explanation: The Ten Commandments express the fundamental duties of love toward God and neighbor; Christ confirmed and deepened them.

clues: I fall fifty days after Easter and close the Easter season.
The disciples were gathered in one place when a sound like a driving wind filled the house.
Tongues as of fire came to rest on each of them, and they spoke in other languages.
The Church calls me her own birthday, the day her mission to the nations began.
items.explanation: At Pentecost the Holy Spirit descended on the apostles, and the Church went out to proclaim the Gospel to all peoples.

clues: God called me to leave my country and my kindred for a land He would show me.
Though my wife and I were far too old, I was promised descendants as countless as the stars.
I was asked to offer my only son on a mountain, and my hand was stayed at the last moment.
St. Paul calls me the father of all who believe.
items.explanation: Abraham's obedient faith made him the father of God's people and the model of trust in the promise.

clues: I called down fire from heaven on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal.
Fed by an angel, I walked forty days to the mountain of God.
There God was not in the wind, the earthquake, or the fire, but in a still small voice.
I was taken up in a whirlwind by a chariot of fire, and I appeared again beside the Lord at the Transfiguration.
items.explanation: Elijah, the great prophet of the northern kingdom, contended for the worship of the one true God and met Him in silence.

clues: In the Temple I saw the Lord high and lifted up, with seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy.'
A burning coal touched my lips, and I said, 'Here I am; send me.'
I foretold a virgin who would conceive and bear a son called Emmanuel.
I described a suffering servant, pierced for our offenses, by whose stripes we are healed.
items.explanation: Isaiah's prophecies of Emmanuel and the Suffering Servant are read by the Church as pointing directly to Christ.

clues: I was a Moabite widow who refused to leave my widowed mother-in-law.
I told her, 'Where you go I will go; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.'
I gleaned in the fields of a kinsman named Boaz, who then redeemed and married me.
My great-grandson was King David, and so I stand in the ancestry of the Messiah.
items.explanation: Ruth, a foreigner grafted into Israel by loyal love, is named in the genealogy of Christ.

clues: I was a Jewish orphan raised by my cousin Mordecai, and I became queen of Persia.
My people faced annihilation by a decree of the king's minister.
I fasted three days, then risked death by approaching the king unbidden.
Mordecai told me I had perhaps come to the kingdom 'for such a time as this.'
items.explanation: Esther's courage and intercession delivered her people from destruction.

clues: My father gave me a long coat, and my brothers hated me for my dreams.
They sold me into Egypt, where I was imprisoned on a false charge.
I interpreted Pharaoh's dreams and was set over all the land to store grain against famine.
When my brothers came begging, I wept and said, 'You meant it for evil, but God meant it for good.'
items.explanation: Joseph, betrayed and exalted, sees God's providence turning even his brothers' malice toward the saving of many.

clues: A captive in Babylon, I refused the king's rich food and kept the law of my God.
I interpreted a dream of a great statue and a stone cut without hands.
For praying to God against a royal decree, I was thrown into a den of lions.
An angel shut the lions' mouths, and in the morning I was found unharmed.
items.explanation: Daniel's fidelity under a hostile power, and his visions of a kingdom that will never be destroyed, sustained Israel's hope.

clues: With my brother James I left the nets, and the Lord called us 'sons of thunder.'
I leaned on His breast at the Last Supper.
I was the only apostle standing at the foot of the cross, and He gave His Mother into my care.
In exile on Patmos I received the visions of the Apocalypse.
items.explanation: John, the beloved disciple, received Mary as his mother at the cross and left the Church a Gospel of the Word made flesh.

clues: When the Lord set out for Judea into danger, I said, 'Let us also go, that we may die with him.'
I was not with the others when the Risen Lord first appeared, and I would not believe their word.
A week later He showed me His hands and His side.
I answered Him, 'My Lord and my God.'
items.explanation: Thomas's demand for proof and his confession 'My Lord and my God' give the Church one of its clearest professions of Christ's divinity.

clues: I was a carpenter of Nazareth, betrothed to a virgin found with child before we came together.
An angel told me in a dream to take her as my wife and to name the child Jesus.
I was warned in another dream to flee with them into Egypt from Herod.
Scripture calls me a just man, and the Gospels record not one word I ever spoke.
items.explanation: Joseph, the just man, guarded and provided for the Holy Family in silent obedience to God's word.

clues: I was a wealthy chief tax collector in Jericho, and short of stature.
To see the Lord pass by, I climbed a sycamore tree.
He looked up and said He must stay at my house that day, and the crowd grumbled.
I pledged half my goods to the poor and fourfold restitution to anyone I had cheated.
items.explanation: Zacchaeus's conversion shows that the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost, and that repentance bears fruit in restitution.

clues: I was crucified beside the Lord, one of two criminals.
I rebuked the other, saying we were justly condemned but this man had done nothing wrong.
I asked only, 'Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.'
He promised me, 'Today you will be with me in Paradise.'
items.explanation: The good thief, canonized by Christ from the cross, shows that a single act of faith and contrition at the end can save.

clues: I was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews who came to the Lord by night.
He told me that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born again of water and the Spirit.
I asked how a man can be born when he is old.
Later I defended Him before the council, and I helped bury Him with about a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes.
items.explanation: To Nicodemus the Lord taught the necessity of baptismal rebirth; Nicodemus moved from a night visit to open devotion at the tomb.

clues: I was a Doctor of the Church who settled in a cave near Bethlehem.
I gave decades to translating the Scriptures into Latin, the version called the Vulgate.
I am often shown in a study with a lion, having drawn a thorn from its paw.
I wrote that ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.
items.explanation: Jerome's Vulgate gave the Latin Church its Bible; the Catechism repeats his warning that to be ignorant of Scripture is to be ignorant of Christ.

clues: My surname means 'golden-mouthed,' for my preaching.
I was archbishop of Constantinople, and my plain rebukes of luxury made me powerful enemies.
I was driven into exile, and I died on the road, saying, 'Glory to God for all things.'
A Divine Liturgy of the Eastern Church still bears my name.
items.explanation: John Chrysostom, Doctor and preacher, taught that Christ is honored at the altar and in the poor at the door alike.

clues: I was bishop of Lyons in the second century, a hearer of Polycarp, who had heard the apostle John.
My great work, Against Heresies, answered the Gnostics point by point.
I taught that Christ 'recapitulates' in Himself the whole history of Adam's race.
I wrote that the glory of God is the living man, and the life of man is the vision of God.
items.explanation: Irenaeus defended the rule of faith handed down from the apostles and the goodness of the created, bodily human person.

clues: I was bishop of Antioch, and I was taken to Rome in chains to be killed for the faith.
On the journey I wrote seven letters to the churches.
I begged the Christians of Rome not to prevent my martyrdom: 'I am God's wheat, to be ground by the teeth of beasts.'
I am the earliest writer known to call the Church 'catholic.'
items.explanation: Ignatius of Antioch bears early witness to the bishop's office, the Eucharist, and the catholic name of the Church, sealed by martyrdom.

clues: The son of a rich cloth merchant, I stripped off my clothes in the square and gave them back to my father.
I heard a crucifix tell me, 'Rebuild my church.'
I embraced Lady Poverty, preached to the birds, and wrote a canticle praising Brother Sun and Sister Moon.
Two years before my death I received the wounds of Christ in my own flesh.
items.explanation: Francis's radical poverty and love for all creation as God's gift made him one of the most beloved of all the saints.

clues: I left my studies in Rome to live as a hermit in a cave at Subiaco.
I founded a monastery on Monte Cassino and wrote a Rule for those who live there.
My Rule is summed up in two words: pray and work.
I am honored as the father of Western monasticism and a patron of Europe.
items.explanation: Benedict's Rule ordered monastic life around prayer, work, and stability, and shaped the civilization of the Christian West.

clues: I was a Spanish Carmelite who reformed my order back to a stricter observance.
I wrote The Interior Castle, describing the soul's journey through seven mansions to union with God.
I said that mental prayer is nothing else than an intimate sharing between friends.
I was the first woman named a Doctor of the Church.
items.explanation: Teresa of Ávila, mystic, reformer, and Doctor, mapped the life of prayer from vocal beginnings to contemplative union.

clues: I was the youngest of many children in a dyer's family, and I became a Dominican tertiary.
Though I never learned to write easily, I dictated a great work called the Dialogue.
I wrote letters to princes and to the pope, urging him to return from Avignon to Rome.
I am a Doctor of the Church and a patron of Italy.
items.explanation: Catherine of Siena combined deep mystical prayer with fearless counsel to the powerful, for the good of the whole Church.

clues: A cannonball shattered my leg at the siege of Pamplona, and I read the lives of the saints while I healed.
At Manresa I wrote a manual of prayer and self-examination called the Spiritual Exercises.
With companions I founded the Society of Jesus.
Our motto is 'for the greater glory of God.'
items.explanation: Ignatius of Loyola turned a soldier's discipline toward God, founding the Jesuits and giving the Church its Spiritual Exercises.

clues: I was a Polish Franciscan who spread devotion to the Immaculata through the press.
I was arrested by the Gestapo and sent to Auschwitz.
When ten men were chosen to die for one prisoner's escape, I stepped forward to take the place of a man with a family.
I died in the starvation bunker, and the man I replaced lived to attend my canonization.
items.explanation: Kolbe's offer of his life for a stranger is a martyr's witness to Christ's own words that no love is greater.

clues: I nearly failed my seminary studies because I could not master Latin.
I was sent to a small, indifferent French village as its parish priest.
People came from across Europe, and I spent up to sixteen hours a day hearing their confessions.
I am the patron saint of parish priests.
items.explanation: The Curé of Ars shows the power of an ordinary priest wholly given to prayer, penance, and the confessional.

clues: I was the first non-Italian pope in over four centuries, elected from behind the Iron Curtain.
My first words to the world were 'Be not afraid.'
I promulgated the Catechism of the Catholic Church in 1992.
I forgave the man who shot me in St. Peter's Square, and I visited him in his cell.
items.explanation: John Paul II's long pontificate gave the Church the current Catechism and a witness of forgiveness and fearless hope.

clues: I am one of the three sacraments of Christian initiation.
The bishop, or a priest he delegates, anoints the forehead with sacred chrism.
The words are: 'Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit.'
I complete baptismal grace and, like Baptism, mark the soul permanently, so I am received only once.
items.explanation: Confirmation seals the baptized with the Holy Spirit, binding them more firmly to the Church and strengthening them to witness.

clues: The Letter of James tells the sick to call the presbyters, who will pray over them and anoint them with oil.
A priest anoints the forehead and hands of the one who is seriously ill or aged.
My effects are the strengthening of the soul, the forgiveness of sins if the person cannot confess, and sometimes bodily healing.
When joined to Viaticum and Confession, I form the Church's 'last rites.'
items.explanation: The Anointing of the Sick unites a person's suffering to Christ's and prepares them for the passage to eternal life.

clues: I am conferred by the laying on of hands and a prayer of consecration by a bishop.
I have three degrees: bishop, priest, and deacon.
Like Baptism and Confirmation, I imprint an indelible character and cannot be repeated.
Through me the apostolic ministry is handed on until the end of time.
items.explanation: Holy Orders continues the mission Christ gave the apostles, configuring the ordained to serve in His name.

clues: The ministers of this sacrament are the spouses themselves; the priest or deacon is the Church's witness.
My essential properties are unity and indissolubility.
The Lord restored me to God's original plan: 'What God has joined together, let no one separate.'
St. Paul calls me a great mystery, a sign of Christ and the Church.
items.explanation: Christ raised the covenant of marriage to a sacrament, an image of His own faithful, fruitful union with the Church.

clues: St. Paul says that if this did not happen, our faith is in vain.
It is attested by the empty tomb and by many appearances to the apostles.
It is celebrated as the greatest of all feasts, and every Sunday is a little instance of it.
By it, death is conquered and the promise of our own bodily rising is guaranteed.
items.explanation: The Resurrection of Christ is the crowning truth of the faith and the ground of Christian hope.

clues: It took place forty days after Easter, on a mountain in the sight of the apostles.
A cloud took Him from their sight, and two men in white asked why they stood gazing up.
By it, Christ's humanity enters definitively into the heavenly glory of God.
He goes to prepare a place, and to send the Spirit.
items.explanation: In the Ascension the risen Christ is seated at the Father's right hand, and human nature is taken up into God's own life.

clues: It happened on a high mountain, with Peter, James, and John.
His face shone like the sun and His clothes became dazzling white.
Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with Him.
A voice from the cloud said, 'This is my beloved Son; listen to him.'
items.explanation: The Transfiguration reveals Christ's divine glory to strengthen the disciples for the scandal of the cross.

clues: I am not a second chance and not the state of the damned.
I am for those who die in God's grace and friendship but are still imperfectly purified.
The living help those here by prayers, almsgiving, and above all the Mass.
Judas Maccabeus made atonement for the dead, that they might be freed from their sin.
items.explanation: Purgatory is the final purification of the elect, wholly different from the punishment of the damned.

clues: I am not chiefly a place but a state: perfect life with the Most Holy Trinity.
Those who reach me see God as He is, face to face.
St. Paul says that what I hold, no eye has seen nor ear heard nor heart conceived.
I am the fulfillment of the deepest longing of every human heart.
items.explanation: Heaven is the blessed community of all who are perfectly incorporated into Christ, seeing God face to face.

clues: The chief punishment I hold is eternal separation from God.
God predestines no one to me; it is entered by a free choice to reject His love and to persist in it to the end.
The Church has never claimed to know of any particular person that they are here.
The Lord's warnings about me are a call to responsibility and conversion now.
items.explanation: Hell is the state of definitive self-exclusion from communion with God, freely chosen and never imposed.

clues: I am a phrase in the Apostles' Creed, right after 'the holy catholic Church.'
I mean the sharing of holy things, above all the Eucharist, and the fellowship of holy persons.
I bind together the faithful on earth, the souls being purified, and the blessed in heaven.
Because of me, we ask the saints to pray for us and we pray for the dead.
items.explanation: The communion of saints is the one Body of Christ, its members on earth, in purgatory, and in glory sharing every spiritual good.

clues: I am a state, not an act, contracted and not committed.
By one man's disobedience, sin and death entered the world and passed to all.
I deprive every descendant of Adam of original holiness, though human nature is wounded, not totally corrupted.
Baptism erases me and turns a person back toward God.
items.explanation: Original sin is the fallen condition all inherit from Adam; Baptism restores the life of grace lost by it.

clues: I begin and end a Christian's prayer, and often the day.
The hand moves from forehead to breast, then shoulder to shoulder.
The words name the three divine persons in whom the Christian was baptized.
I mark the body with the instrument of our redemption.
items.explanation: The Sign of the Cross professes the Trinity and claims the whole person for Christ crucified.

clues: St. Paul told the Thessalonians to stand firm and hold to what he taught 'by word of mouth or by letter.'
I am not a set of extra facts but the living transmission of the whole Gospel in the Church.
Together with Scripture I flow from the same divine wellspring and make up one sacred deposit.
The Magisterium serves me; it is not above me.
items.explanation: Sacred Tradition is the Gospel handed on in the life, teaching, and worship of the Church, inseparable from Scripture.

clues: I open the Sermon on the Mount, and there are eight of me.
Each of my lines begins with the same word: 'Blessed.'
I promise the kingdom to the poor in spirit and the vision of God to the pure of heart.
I paint the portrait of Christ Himself and the path of Christian happiness.
items.explanation: The Beatitudes reveal the goal of human existence and the face of Christ, calling the disciple to a blessedness the world cannot give.
